description: Krypton is a colorless, odorless noble gas with atomic number 36 that occurs in trace amounts in the atmosphere. It is chemically inert and was discovered in Britain in 1898 by William Ramsay and Morris Travers from residue left after evaporating liquid air.
uses: Krypton is used in fluorescent lamps, high-powered gas lasers, and photography as a white light source. It is also used in incandescent lamps to reduce filament evaporation, in krypton fluoride lasers for nuclear fusion research, in electromagnetic calorimeters for particle physics, in magnetic resonance imaging, and as an insulating gas between window panes and as a propellant in electric propulsion systems.
characteristics: Krypton is characterized by several sharp emission lines with the strongest being green and yellow. Solid krypton is white and has a face-centered cubic crystal structure. It is one of the products of uranium fission and is highly volatile, not staying in solution in near-surface water.
